abstract: We consider the quantum time complexity of the all pairs shortest paths (APSP) problem and some of its variants. The trivial classical algorithm for APSP and most all pairs path problems runs in $O(n^{3})$ time, while the trivial algorithm in the quantum setting runs in $\tilde{O}(n^{2.5})$ time, using Grover search. A major open problem in classical algorithms is to obtain a truly subcubic time algorithm for APSP, i.e. an algorithm running in $O(n^{3-\varepsilon})$ time for constant $\varepsilon>0$. To approach this problem, many truly subcubic time classical algorithms have been devised for APSP and its variants for structured inputs. Some examples of such problems are APSP in geometrically weighted graphs, graphs with small integer edge weights or a small number of weights incident to each vertex, and the all pairs earliest arrivals problem. In this paper we revisit these problems in the quantum setting and obtain the first nontrivial (i.e. $O(n^{2.5-\varepsilon})$ time) quantum algorithms for the problems.

specification.problem: All pairs shortest paths (APSP): given a weighted graph G=(V,E,w) with |V|=n and no negative cycles, compute the distance matrix d(i,j) for all vertex pairs. The abstract claims the first quantum algorithms running in O(n^{2.5-\varepsilon}) time for structured variants (geometrically weighted graphs, small integer weights, few distinct weights per vertex, all pairs earliest arrivals), improving on the trivial Grover-based \tilde{O}(n^{2.5}) algorithm.
specification.reconstruction_scope: The abstract gives no construction details for the paper's O(n^{2.5-\varepsilon}) algorithms. Scope is therefore restricted to the baseline the abstract explicitly references: the trivial \tilde{O}(n^{2.5}) quantum APSP algorithm, reconstructed as repeated (min,+) matrix squaring where each entry minimum is computed with Dürr–Høyer quantum minimum finding (Grover search with a threshold oracle). The circuit-level unit is a single Grover-marked threshold search over the summation index k for one fixed entry (i,j) and threshold t. Tiny instance: an undirected 4-vertex graph with weights w(0,1)=1, w(1,2)=1, w(0,2)=3, w(2,3)=1, w(1,3)=5 (non-edges = INF), so that two squarings are needed to obtain d(0,3)=3. OUTSIDE SCOPE (paper contributions not reconstructable from the abstract): the actual subcubic-improving quantum algorithms for geometric weights, small integer weights, bounded weights per vertex, and earliest arrivals, and the values of \varepsilon achieved.

equations.label: APSP distance definition
equations.description: Shortest path distance as the minimum total weight over all i-to-j paths; d(i,i)=0 and d(i,j)=\infty if no path exists.
equations.justification: Standard definition of the APSP problem named in the abstract.
assumptions: No negative cycles (nonnegative weights assumed in the tiny instance)

equations.label: (min,+) product and repeated squaring
equations.description: Exact equality: \lceil\log_2(n-1)\rceil successive (min,+) squarings of the weight matrix yield the distance matrix, since shortest paths use at most n-1 edges. For n=4, s=2.
equations.justification: Classical textbook reduction of APSP to O(\log n) (min,+) products; chosen here as the structure of the trivial baseline.
assumptions: Nonnegative weights so shortest paths are simple

equations.label: Threshold oracle for one entry (i,j)
equations.description: Boolean oracle marking intermediate vertices k that improve the current threshold t for entry (i,j). With the flag qubit prepared in |-\rangle this acts as a phase oracle (-1)^{f_t(k)}. The matrix entries are classical data; the oracle is assumed implementable in \tilde{O}(1) time (QRAM-type access).
equations.justification: Standard marking oracle used by Dürr–Høyer minimum finding; the quantities compared come from eq_2.
assumptions: Classical data accessible in superposition in polylog time (QRAM model)

equations.label: Grover iterate and iteration count
equations.description: Grover iterate with diffusion over the index register; M_t is the (unknown) number of marked indices, so in practice the exponential-search schedule of Boyer–Brassard–Høyer–Tapp is used (random r in a growing range). This is an approximation: success probability is high but not 1.
equations.justification: The abstract attributes the trivial \tilde{O}(n^{2.5}) bound to Grover search; this is the standard Grover iterate and count.
assumptions: n is not necessarily a power of 2; if not, pad the index register and mark padding indices as 0

equations.label: Quantum minimum finding and baseline cost
equations.latex: \min_{k}\big(D^{(\ell)}_{ik}+D^{(\ell)}_{kj}\big)\ \text{found with}\ O(\sqrt{n})\ \text{oracle queries (expected)},\qquad T_{\text{trivial}}=n^{2}\cdot O(\sqrt{n})\cdot\lceil\log_2 n\rceil=\tilde{O}(n^{2.5})
equations.description: Dürr–Høyer: repeated Grover threshold search with t updated to the last found value uses O(\sqrt{n}) expected queries. Applying it to all n^2 entries over O(\log n) squarings gives the trivial \tilde{O}(n^{2.5}) quantum APSP algorithm cited in the abstract.
equations.abstract_quote: the trivial algorithm in the quantum setting runs in $\tilde{O}(n^{2.5})$ time, using Grover search
equations.justification: The abstract states the trivial quantum bound and its Grover origin; the decomposition into n^2 entries times \sqrt{n} minimum finding times \log n squarings is one standard way to realize it (an alternative is Dijkstra per source with quantum SSSP).
assumptions: QRAM access to the current matrix

equations.label: Paper's claimed improvement (not reconstructed)
equations.description: Target running time for the structured APSP variants. The abstract provides no algorithmic details enabling reconstruction of how this bound is achieved.
equations.abstract_quote: obtain the first nontrivial (i.e. $O(n^{2.5-\varepsilon})$ time) quantum algorithms for the problems

registers.name: idx
registers.role: Search index k over intermediate vertices; big-endian binary encoding of k

registers.name: flag
registers.role: Oracle output qubit, prepared in |-\rangle so the oracle acts as a phase oracle

registers.name: anc
registers.role: Work qubits for computing D_{ik}+D_{kj} and comparing with t; uncomputed after each oracle call

specification.initial_state: |0\rangle^{\otimes\lceil\log_2 n\rceil}|1\rangle on (idx, flag); after H^{\otimes\lceil\log_2 n\rceil}\otimes H this is |\psi\rangle|-\rangle with |\psi\rangle the uniform superposition over k (eq_4). Classical data: D^{(1)} for the tiny instance with rows [0,1,3,INF],[1,0,1,5],[3,1,0,1],[INF,5,1,0].

steps.description: Classical outer loop: set D^{(1)} to the weight matrix with zero diagonal; repeat the squaring step s=\lceil\log_2(n-1)\rceil times (s=2 for n=4).
For each entry (i,j), run quantum minimum finding: initialize threshold t=\infty (or a random index's value); prepare idx in uniform superposition and flag in |-\rangle.
Apply the threshold oracle O_t^{(i,j)} and the diffusion operator r times (r chosen by the exponential-search schedule since the number of marked indices is unknown).

Measure idx, obtain k'; classically verify f_t(k')=1 (compute D_{ik'}+D_{k'j}<t); if so set t to this value and repeat from the superposition preparation; stop after the Dürr–Høyer budget of O(\sqrt{n}) total queries and output the final t as (D\star D)_{ij}.
Assemble the new matrix D^{(2\ell)} from all n^2 entries; after s squarings return it as the APSP distance matrix (e.g., d(0,3)=3 in the tiny instance via 0\to1\to2\to3).

specification.measurement: Computational-basis measurement of the idx register after each Grover search round; outcome k' is a candidate intermediate vertex. The flag and ancilla registers are discarded (ancillas uncomputed).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Verify each measured candidate classically by computing D_{ik'}+D_{k'j} and comparing with the threshold t; update t to the improved value; after the query budget is exhausted the last threshold is the entry minimum (correct with high probability, not deterministically). Collect all n^2 entries into the squared matrix and iterate the squaring s times.
assumptions: No experiment_scope was provided; the chosen construction is the trivial Grover-based \tilde{O}(n^{2.5}) baseline via (min,+) squaring with Dürr–Høyer minimum finding, not the paper's improved algorithms.
Tiny instance choice: undirected graph on 4 vertices with weights w(0,1)=1, w(1,2)=1, w(0,2)=3, w(2,3)=1, w(1,3)=5, non-edges INF.
Nonnegative edge weights so shortest paths are simple and have at most n-1 edges.
QRAM-style superposition access to classical matrix entries in polylogarithmic time, as is standard for Grover-based graph algorithms.
Quantum minimum finding succeeds with high (not unit) probability; running times are expected/with-high-probability bounds.
